from.place: Comparator challenge theorem WeilConjectures.weil_conjectures (lean/Comparator/Weil/Challenge.lean): factorization, functional equation and Riemann hypothesis for smooth proper geometrically integral X over a finite field

title: WeilConjectures.weil_conjectures
statement:
Let k be a finite field with q=#k elements, d a natural number, and f:X->Spec k a morphism of schemes that is smooth of relative dimension d, proper and geometrically integral [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]. For a finite field k with q=#k elements, a scheme X and a morphism f:X->Spec k, the zeta series Z(X,t)=f.zetaSeries in Q[[t]] [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] is Z(X,t)=exp(sum_{n>=1} N_n t^n/n), substituted into the formal exponential series, where N_n=f.pointCount n is the number of k-morphisms Spec F_{q^n} -> X (morphisms g with g followed by f equal to the map induced by k -> F_{q^n}), F_{q^n} being the model FiniteField.galoisExtension k n = the splitting field over k of X^{q^n}-X, and N_n=0 (junk value) if this set is infinite. A polynomial with integer coefficients is viewed in Q[[t]] through its coefficientwise image in Q[t] [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension, def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. Then there is a family P_0,...,P_{2d} in Z[t] [def-weil-polynomial-ring], indexed by i in {0,...,2d}, with the three properties:
(1) Weil factorization (IsWeilFactorization q d Z P): P_i(0)=1 for every i [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]; P_0=1-t; P_{2d}=1-q^d t; and Z(X,t) * prod_{i even} P_i = prod_{i odd} P_i in Q[[t]] [def-weil-formal-power-series].
(2) Functional equation (WeilFunctionalEquation q d P): for every i, the multiset of complex roots of P_{2d-i} (roots of its coefficientwise image in C[t], counted with multiplicity) [def-weil-polynomial-root, def-weil-root-multiplicity] equals the image of the multiset of complex roots of P_i under z |-> (q^d z)^{-1}.
(3) Riemann hypothesis (WeilRiemannHypothesis q d P): for every i and every complex root z of P_i, |z| = q^{-i/2} (real power) [def-weil-complex-absolute-value, def-weil-real-power].
Equivalently the inverse roots alpha of P_i are q^{i/2}-Weil numbers and alpha |-> q^d/alpha matches the inverse roots of P_i with those of P_{2d-i}.

lean.statement:
theorem weil_conjectures (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [IsProper f]
    [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
    ∃ P : Fin (2 * d + 1) → Polynomial ℤ,
      IsWeilFactorization (Nat.card k) d f.zetaSeries P ∧
      WeilFunctionalEquation (Nat.card k) d P ∧
      WeilRiemannHypothesis (Nat.card k) d P
